definitions.explanation: The act of yielding a point or making a compromise in a negotiation or argument. Implies making a sacrifice or giving up something to reach an agreement.

examples.japanese: {譲歩|じょうほ}を{求|もと}める
{相手|あいて}の{譲歩|じょうほ}を{引|ひ}き{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I managed to get a concession from the other party.

examples.japanese: {双方|そうほう}が{譲歩|じょうほ}しなければ、{交渉|こうしょう}は{成立|せいりつ}しない。
examples.english: Unless both sides make concessions, the negotiations will not succeed.

notes:
USAGE: Used as a noun or with する to form the verb {譲歩|じょうほ}する (to make a concession, to compromise).

NUANCE: {譲歩|じょうほ} implies a deliberate decision to give ground or make sacrifices, typically in formal negotiations. It often appears in business and diplomatic contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {譲歩|じょうほ}する (to make a concession)
- {譲歩|じょうほ}を{求|もと}める (to demand a concession)
- {譲歩|じょうほ}を{引|ひ}き{出|だ}す (to extract a concession)
- {相互|そうご}{譲歩|じょうほ} (mutual compromise)
- {大幅|おおはば}な{譲歩|じょうほ} (significant concession)

RELATED WORDS:
- {妥協|だきょう} (compromise - more general, everyday use)
- {折|お}り{合|あ}い (compromise, settlement)
- {歩|あゆ}み{寄|よ}り (meeting halfway)
